stimulus:
I will arise and go now, and go to Innisfree,
And a small cabin build there, of clay and wattles made;
Nine bean-rows will I have there, a hive for the honey-bee,
And live alone in the bee-loud glade.

And I shall have some peace there, for peace comes dropping slow,
Dropping from the veils of the morning to where the cricket sings;
There midnight's all a glimmer, and noon a purple glow,
And evening full of the linnet's wings.

I will arise and go now, for always night and day
I hear lake water lapping with low sounds by the shore;
While I stand on the roadway, or on the pavements grey,
I hear it in the deep heart's core.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus, persistent AP-1 chromatin occupancy (the 'deep heart's core' echo)
ideas.description: Pulse cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) with a stimulus such as TNF, PMA or wounding, then wash out and track AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding by CUT&RUN and chromatin accessibility by ATAC-seq at days 0, 1, 7 and 21. Like the lake water still heard on grey pavements long after leaving the shore, memory would show up as retained accessible AP-1 motif sites after the stimulus and the FOS/JUN transcripts have decayed.

ideas.title: Acute degron depletion to separate initiation from maintenance
ideas.description: Use auxin-inducible degradation of FOS or JUN (or dominant-negative A-FOS) at different times: before, during, or after the priming stimulus. If AP-1 is only needed during priming but memory persists, it initiates memory. If depleting it after priming erases accessibility and the faster secondary response, it maintains memory.

ideas.title: Primed-versus-naive re-stimulation response with motif-site mutagenesis
ideas.description: Measure the transcriptional response (nascent RNA, PRO-seq) to a second stimulus in primed and naive cells, and identify the genes with enhanced responses. Then use CRISPR to mutate or dCas9-block the AP-1 motifs at selected enhancers to test whether those sites are necessary for the enhanced response. Add a reporter-based test of whether the primed state is cis-encoded.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics and heritability across divisions
ideas.description: Track endogenous FOS/JUN with fluorescent knock-in tags and AP-1 reporters in single cells through time, lineage-tracing after stimulus. Test whether state is inherited by daughter cells and decays over a characteristic number of divisions, as expected for epigenetic memory, rather than reflecting continued signaling. Relate the dynamics, such as pulsatile versus sustained, to the memory outcome.

ideas.title: Chromatin-state coupling: AP-1 with BAF and histone marks, plus in vivo test
ideas.description: Test whether AP-1 recruits BAF remodelers and deposits H3K27ac or H3K4me1 that persist, using BRG1 inhibition, ChIP/CUT&Tag and sequential perturbation. Then check in vivo, for example in skin or after inflammation, whether tissue cells retain AP-1-dependent accessible regions weeks after injury and respond faster on re-challenge.
